column1: # Longest grapheme match, deliberately small deterministic prototype
# Context rules: ^ marks a word start, $ a word end, and - a silent grapheme.
# Deterministic prototype only; a declared pronunciation always outranks it.
# A plural -s after a vowel and y is voiced: days 데이즈, boys 보이즈 (2026-10-02).
# Second pass: common English word shapes in Korean scripts.
# A "." is a morpheme boundary: up+loading keeps 업, not 어플.
# A word-final syllabic l has no vowel of its own: simple 심플, enable 이네이블.
# Neighbours of the rules above, so one word does not own a rule.
# An s between vowels is voiced: season 시즌, music 뮤직, easy 이지.
